title: Unsupervised Domain Adaptation for Cross-Water Underwater Acoustic Target Recognition: A Four-Corpus Benchmark on Oceanship, QiandaoEar22, an AIS-Auto-Labeled VTUAD Reconstruction, and ShipsEar
content: Underwater acoustic target recognition (UATR) models collapse when moved across bodies of water, and unsupervised domain adaptation (UDA) is the standard remedy when the target water has no labels. We benchmark four UDA paradigms—source-only training, correlation alignment (CORAL), multi-kernel MMD, and domain-adversarial training (DANN, CDAN)—against a supervised target oracle on a frozen two-class protocol spanning four corpora: open-ocean Oceanship, freshwater-lake QiandaoEar22, an AIS-auto-labeled VTUAD reconstruction, and nearshore ShipsEar (40 method–direction combinations × three seeds (120 runs), strict source-validation model selection, paired significance tests; DANN/CDAN on the two-domain matrix only). Adaptation works but is strongly direction-asymmetric. In the lake→ocean direction, MMD lifts macro-F1 from 0.358 (majority-class collapse) to 0.593 ± 0.056, recovering 83% of the supervised oracle and restoring passenger-ship recall from 0/1,214 to up to 662/1,214. The ocean→lake direction is oracle-locked by an 89-segment minority test class; there UDA's measurable value is accuracy-variance compression (F(2,2) ≤ 0.153) and class-bias correction. Moment matching is consistently more stable than adversarial training, whose conditional variant CDAN shows direction-dependent early-stopping collapse. The VTUAD third domain reverses the moment-matching ranking—CORAL becomes most reliable—and MMD produces the study's first significant negative adaptation (−0.190 macro-F1, p = 0.008). On the hardest ShipsEar direction all methods fail (macro-F1 ≤ 0.186 vs. 0.8356 chance). We release the MMSI-retaining VTUAD pipeline, code, frozen splits, and per-seed results.
